ios.desc:
TriLog is the personal data logger.

Capture mood, energy, focus, and symptoms in seconds — then see how they line up with sleep, weather, habits, and everything else on one timeline.

Most trackers ask once a day how you felt, then average it. But the crash hits at 2pm. The migraine lasts four hours. The good morning follows a bad night. TriLog records moments, not daily summaries: every entry has a time, and a whole week sits on one screen, hour by hour.

Built for people who already track seriously — energy you have to budget, symptoms nobody can explain, experiments you're running on yourself — and who have outgrown mood journals, spreadsheets, and scattered notes.

NEW IN 4.0

• Notes view — every note, tracker entry, and dose from the week in one place. Filter it, or flip to a two-week time-of-day chart.
• Forms — log several fields as one entry: a pain episode, a bowel event, a restaurant visit. Start from a template or build your own.
• Trials — run an experiment (magnesium, no afternoon coffee), mark the days you missed, then end it Adopted, Dropped, or Inconclusive.
• Episode trackers — a headache with a start, a severity, and a stop, drawn as a band for as long as it lasted.
• Provider Report — a printable PDF of your sleep, energy, trackers, and forms to bring to an appointment.
• Interactive dashboards — export the week chart or your metrics as a web page and explore months on a big screen.
• Trio view — a week chart with the three columns you choose.

CAPTURE IN SECONDS

Capture has to be effortless or it won't survive a hard week.

• One tap each for mood, energy, and activity
• Quick Track — leave it open and log with single taps
• Type a line — "t hd 3", "int coffee" — with your own shorthand
• Siri — "energy 3", "mood sad"
• Long-press any chart to log at that time; drag a marker to re-time it

EVERYTHING ON ONE CLOCK

Your entries sit alongside weather, barometric pressure, pollen, air quality, and daylight; Apple Health sleep stages, HRV, resting heart rate, steps, and workouts; and hour-by-hour Screen Time. Did this week feel worse because of sleep, pressure, screen time, or something you took on Tuesday?

WHAT YOU CAN LOG

• Mood, energy, and activity throughout the day
• Notes — meals with calories, health, journal, cycle
• Trackers — ratings, numbers, choices, episodes, traffic lights, titled ratings
• Intake — coffee, supplements, medications, with caffeine totaled in mg
• Day Launch and Day End — sleep, goals, reflections, routine

quotes.text:
I think this one is a bit different, faster/easier to input and an information dense display.

I'm a software engineer with 25 years of experience, and this started as something I built for myself. I originally wanted to track energy and didn’t find something in the App Store that fit what I had in mind.  I prototyped the first version in Rork, which got me moving fast, then migrated to Xcode when I needed more control over proprietary extensions.I’ve been using it daily for several months while I add features and rearrange things. I’m just starting to promote it now.

The main screen shows your whole week at a glance as a color grid, so you can spot patterns without navigating through multiple screens. Data stays private on your device and backs up to your personal iCloud. No sign-in, no shared database. All of the important features are free and there are no ads. There is a subscription for some extra features.

Feedback and bug reports welcome! I’m hoping some others will find it as useful as I do.
